summary.title: Honeypot Deployment: Threat Model
summary.description: This threat model covers a network-based honeypot deployed to detect and analyze unauthorized access attempts. The primary concern in scope is containment: if an attacker who compromises the honeypot is able to move laterally into other parts of the network, this could expose production systems, internal credentials, or sensitive data, potentially leading to broader compromise of the organization's infrastructure. The model evaluates the honeypot's network segmentation, monitoring, and isolation controls to assess how well it prevents this kind of pivot.

data.name: Protected Asset Zone (Protected By ACL configurations)

threats.title: No MFA org Router SSH
threats.description: An external attacker who has scanned the network for exposed management services can target the Org Router's SSH interface, and if there is no MFA configured they may perform brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks to get themselves into an authenticated session; once inside, they can view or alter routing configuration, compromising the organisation's very first point of network control and gaining a foothold for further internal reconnaissance.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA on router management; use key-based auth over passwords

threats.title: Org Router Firewall Misconfiguration
threats.description: An external attacker probing the network perimeter can send traffic that should be blocked by the Org Router's firewall but is instead permitted due to overly permissive rules, allowing them to reach further into the internal network than intended and bypassing the organisation's first layer of perimeter defense
threats.mitigation: Regularly audit firewall rulesets; apply default-deny with explicit allow rules only for required traffic

threats.title: New STRIDE threat
threats.description: Provide a description for this threat
threats.mitigation: Provide remediation for this threat or a reason if status is N/A

threats.title: Weak/Defualt Credentials
threats.description: If the device still has defualt or weak management credentials , an attacker could gain unauthorised access ,once in, they could view or alter routing and firewall configurations
threats.mitigation: Change all default credentials before deployment. Enforce strong, unique passwords per device, and combine this with MFA

threats.title: No MFA on L2 Switch Management SSH
threats.description: An attacker who has already obtained credentials, either through reconnaissance or a prior compromise, can authenticate to the L2 Switch's SSH management interface without needing a second factor, then modify switch configuration such as VLAN assignments or port security, potentially opening a path for VLAN hopping between the isolated Honeypot zone and the organisation's trusted network
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA on switch management access; restrict to IT or VLAN only

threats.title: Weak or Default Credentials
threats.description: If the L2 Switch still has default or easily guessed management credentials, an attacker could gain unauthorised access into the network.Once in, they could alter switch configuration such as VLAN assignments or port security, potentially opening a path for VLAN hopping between the Honeypot zone and the organisation's trusted network.
threats.mitigation: Change all default credentials on the L2 Switch before deployment. Enforce a strong, unique password, and combine this with MFA

threats.title: Honeypot Fingerprinting
threats.description: An external attacker actively probing the honeypot after gaining initial access may notice inconsistencies such as VM artifacts, mismatched service banners, or unnaturally clean traffic patterns, allowing them to conclude they're interacting with a honeypot rather than a real production host; once this happens, the attacker can deliberately shape their behaviour to feed misleading data into the collection pipeline, undermining the integrity of the entire research dataset.
threats.mitigation: Harden honeypot to reduce detectable artifacts; monitor for reconnaissance behaviour indicating fingerprinting attempts

threats.title: Denial of Service on Honeypot System
threats.description: Once an attacker has fingerprinted the honeypot and realised they're being observed, they may flood or exhaust the system's resources purely to cause disruption rather than pursue further access, halting data collection for the duration of the outage and leaving gaps in the CTI dataset the research depends on.
threats.mitigation: Monitor honeypot availability and alert on unexpected service interruption, since the outage itself is a detection signal

threats.title: Unpatched honeypot service exploited for full compromise/privilege escalation
threats.description: An attacker who identifies an unpatched or outdated service running on the honeypot can exploit a known vulnerability to gain remote code execution, escalating from initial access to full system compromise and potentially a higher level of control than the exposed service should allow
threats.mitigation: Research and fully understand each service running on the honeypot, including how it could be exploited. Assess whether a successful exploit would give the attacker a foothold into more critical parts of the network, such as Production or Monitoring. If it would, patch it before the honeypot goes live, If it wouldn't, it can be left as-is, since it's meant to be exploitable for CTI collection.

threats.title: Fingerprinting-Driven False Telemetry
threats.description: After fingerprinting the honeypot, an attacker can deliberately perform misleading actions that get logged as legitimate attacker behaviour; the organisation, working from this poisoned data, may design mitigations around a flawed picture of the threat, and because the attacker is aware of what mitigation was applied, they can exploit the resulting predictable gap later, damaging both the research's data integrity and the organisation's actual defensive posture.
threats.mitigation: Cross-validate honeypot findings against independent detection sources (e.g. compare Suricata vs. Zeek results) before acting on them; treat honeypot data as a signal, not sole justification, for mitigation decisions

threats.title: Honeypot Log tampering
threats.description: If an attacker can successfully pivot into the Monitoring VLAN by crossing the boundary, they can gain access to the Honeypot Logs data store and alter or delete stored TTP data, erasing evidence of their own activity and directly invalidating the evidentiary base the research's findings are built on
threats.mitigation: Write-once/append-only log storage; separate log storage host from analysis host; regular integrity hashing of log files

data.name: Decoy PC
data.description: This PC allows for us to see the attacker's lateral movement within the Honeypot VLAN

threats.title: Denial of Serive on Decoy PC
threats.description: An attacker who has pivoted from the honeypot toward the Decoy PC may flood or crash it simply for disruption rather than strategic gain, which removes the ability to observe and evidence lateral movement, weakening the research's core claim that a pivot between systems is possible.
threats.mitigation: Monitor Decoy PC availability and treat unexpected downtime as evidence of an attacker attempting to disrupt lateral-movement detection

threats.title: No MFA on L3 Switch Management SSH
threats.description: An attacker who has obtained switch credentials, whether externally or after pivoting from another compromised device, can log into the L3 Switch's SSH management interface without a second factor and alter routing or ACL configuration, compromising the very device responsible for enforcing segmentation between the Honeypot VLAN and the organisation's Protected Asset Zone.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA on switch management access; restrict management interface to an out-of-band network

threats.title: Routing Table Exposure via L3 Switch
threats.description: Having compromised management access to the L3 Switch, an attacker can read its routing tables and discover that a Production VLAN exists along with its IP addressing, giving them the reconnaissance information needed to deliberately target the production system
threats.mitigation: Restrict management interface access; disable unnecessary services that could leak routing data

threats.title: ACL and Firewall Misconfiguration Enabling Boundary Crossing
threats.description: Armed with the routing knowledge gained from exposing the L3 Switch's tables, an attacker can send traffic across a misconfigured ACL at the boundary between the Honeypot VLAN and the Protected Asset Zone, crossing undetected into the organisation's trusted network and defeating the core segmentation control the entire containment design relies on
threats.mitigation: Regularly audit and test ACL rules; apply least-privilege segmentation between VLANs

threats.title: Weak or Default Credentials
threats.description: If the Layer Switch, still has default or easily guessed management credentials, an attacker could gain unauthorised, once in, they could view or alter routing and ACL configuration.
threats.mitigation: Change all default credentials on the device before deployment. Enforce strong, unique passwords on the device, and combine this with MFA

data.name: ACL deny -L3 switch enforces no attcker/honeypot VLAN or LAN to Production but other traffic is allowed

threats.title: Unencrypted Data in Transit
threats.description: An attacker with visibility into the link between the L3 and L2 Switch, sitting right at the segmentation boundary, can intercept this unencrypted traffic and read its contents in plaintext, exposing data at the exact point meant to separate the Honeypot VLAN from the organisation's trusted zone
threats.mitigation: Encrypt data in transit using strong encryption standards

threats.title: No integrity Checks on data flow
threats.description: Lacking integrity verification, the data flow between the L3 and L2 Switch is vulnerable to an attacker altering traffic in transit at the segmentation boundary itself without detection, undermining confidence that traffic entering the trusted zone is legitimate and unmodified
threats.mitigation: Implement integrity verification such as hashing/signing

labels: ACL deny -L3 switch enforces no attcker/honeypot VLAN or LAN to Production but other traffic is allowed

data.name: DF between R and L3 S

threats.title: Unencrypted Data in Transit
threats.description: If data flow is not encrypted, an attacker with visibility into this  link could read traffic contents in plaintext, which exposes internal traffic content and topology details , which aids in further reconnaissance toward other systems in the internal network
threats.mitigation: Encrypt data in transit using strong encryption standards

threats.title: No Integrity Checks on Data Flows
threats.description: If the data flow between the Org Router and L3 Switch has no integrity verification, an attacker with access to this link can alter the traffic in transit without either endpoint being compromised and without the tampering being detected
threats.mitigation: Implement integrity verification hashing/signing on data flows.

threats.title: Unencrypted Data in Transit
threats.description: An attacker who has pivoted into the Monitoring VLAN and gained visibility into its link with the L2 Switch can intercept this unencrypted traffic and read its contents in plaintext, potentially exposing SIEM configuration and detection capability that would otherwise remain hidden from them
threats.mitigation: Encrypt data in transit using strong encryption standards

threats.title: No integrity Checks on Data Flow
threats.description: Without integrity verification on the data flow between Monitoring and the L2 Switch, an attacker with access to this link can alter monitoring traffic in transit undetected, compromising the reliability of the data the research dataset depends on.
threats.mitigation: Implement integrity verification such as hashing/signing on critical data flow

threats.title: Production Network Compromise
threats.description: Having successfully crossed the boundary via the ACL misconfiguration, an attacker can leverage their established foothold to reach Production systems directly, gaining access to sensitive company data, escalating privileges, and potentially disrupting or crippling production operations
threats.mitigation: Defense-in-depth: network segmentation, monitoring alerts on cross-VLAN traffic, incident response plan for breach containment, strict ACL configuration and verification

data.name: Protected from attacker and honeypot via ACL config (ACL deny)

threats.title: Unencrypted Data in Transit
threats.description: An attacker with visibility into the link between the L2 Switch and Production, gained through prior compromise, can intercept this unencrypted traffic and read sensitive company data in plaintext
threats.mitigation: Encrypt data in transit using strong encryption standards.

threats.title: No integrity Checks on Data flow
threats.description: If the data flow between the L2 Switch and Production lacks integrity verification, an attacker with access to this link can alter production-bound traffic in transit without detection, risking corrupted or manipulated data reaching production systems and undermining data integrity for business operations.
threats.mitigation: Implement integrity verification such as hashing/signing
